learning_outcomes.text: Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

Knowledge of the fundamental principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation and analysis of pipes, channels, and fluid transport systems.
Knowledge of basic, scientific, and technological subjects that allow continuous learning, as well as the ability to adapt to new situations and changing environments.

syllabus_topics: Density, Specific Volume, and Relative Density
Appendix: Tables of Moments of Inertia and Centers of Gravity
Introduction to Flow in Closed Conduits
Fully Developed Laminar Flow in a Pipe
Fully Developed Turbulent Flow in a Pipe
Concept of Geometric, Piezometric, and Total Head Lines
Four Basic Problems of Pipe Calculation
teaching_methods: Participatory master class, conferences, company visits, fair attendance, etc.
Individual or group resolution of cases, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics (Laboratory).
Completion of a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities (Integrated Project).

Personalized and small group attention. Instruction aimed at reviewing, reorienting class materials, learning, and completing assignments, etc. Specific student inquiries. Scheduled tutorials (Tutoring).
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects, etc. For submission and presentation in practical classes (Group Work).
Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, elaboration of exercises, class preparation, etc. (Individual Work).
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on written tests (60%), practical reports/problems (10%), observation (5%), and an integrated project (25%, including oral defense and project). To average with other components, written tests must be passed with a grade higher than 4 out of 10. The course is passed if the final grade is 5 or higher, and no written part grade is below 4. In the first call, failed parts can be retaken; in the second call, integrated project grades are maintained.
